rows.text: Knowing that this body is (fragile) like a jar, and making this thought firm like a fortress, one should attack Mara (the tempter) with the weapon of knowledge, one should watch him when conquered, and should never rest.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Before long, alas! this body will lie on the earth, despised, without understanding, like a useless log.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Whatever a hater may do to a hater, or an enemy to an enemy, a wrongly-directed mind will do us greater mischief.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Not a mother, not a father will do so much, nor any other relative; a well-directed mind will do us greater service.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Who shall overcome this earth, and the world of Yama (the lord of the departed), and the world of the gods? Who shall find out the plainly shown path of virtue, as a clever man finds out the (right) flower?
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The disciple will overcome the earth, and the world of Yama, and the world of the gods. The disciple will find out the plainly shown path of virtue, as a clever man finds out the (right) flower.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who knows that this body is like froth, and has learnt that it is as unsubstantial as a mirage, will break the flower-pointed arrow of Mara, and never see the king of death.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Death carries off a man who is gathering flowers and whose mind is distracted, as a flood carries off a sleeping village.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Death subdues a man who is gathering flowers, and whose mind is distracted, before he is satiated in his pleasures.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: As the bee collects nectar and departs without injuring the flower, or its colour or scent, so let a sage dwell in his village.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Not the perversities of others, not their sins of commission or omission, but his own misdeeds and negligences should a sage take notice of.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Like a beautiful flower, full of colour, but without scent, are the fine but fruitless words of him who does not act accordingly.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: But, like a beautiful flower, full of colour and full of scent, are the fine and fruitful words of him who acts accordingly.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: As many kinds of wreaths can be made from a heap of flowers, so many good things may be achieved by a mortal when once he is born.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The scent of flowers does not travel against the wind, nor (that of) sandal-wood, or of Tagara and Mallika flowers; but the odour of good people travels even against the wind; a good man pervades every place.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Sandal-wood or Tagara, a lotus-flower, or a Vassiki, among these sorts of perfumes, the perfume of virtue is unsurpassed.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Mean is the scent that comes from Tagara and sandal-wood;--the perfume of those who possess virtue rises up to the gods as the highest.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Of the people who possess these virtues, who live without thoughtlessness, and who are emancipated through true knowledge, Mara, the tempter, never finds the way. 58, 59. As on a heap of rubbish cast upon the highway the lily will grow full of sweet perfume and delight, thus the disciple of the truly enlightened Buddha shines forth by his knowledge among those who are like rubbish, among the people that walk in darkness.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Long is the night to him who is awake; long is a mile to him who is tired; long is life to the foolish who do not know the true law.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If a traveller does not meet with one who is his better, or his equal, let him firmly keep to his solitary journey; there is no companionship with a fool.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: "These sons belong to me, and this wealth belongs to me," with such thoughts a fool is tormented. He himself does not belong to himself; how much less sons and wealth?
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The fool who knows his foolishness, is wise at least so far. But a fool who thinks himself wise, he is called a fool indeed.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If a fool be associated with a wise man even all his life, he will perceive the truth as little as a spoon perceives the taste of soup.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If an intelligent man be associated for one minute only with a wise man, he will soon perceive the truth, as the tongue perceives the taste of soup.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Fools of little understanding have themselves for their greatest enemies, for they do evil deeds which must bear bitter fruits.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: That deed is not well done of which a man must repent, and the reward of which he receives crying and with a tearful face.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: No, that deed is well done of which a man does not repent, and the reward of which he receives gladly and cheerfully.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: As long as the evil deed done does not bear fruit, the fool thinks it is like honey; but when it ripens, then the fool suffers grief.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Let a fool month after month eat his food (like an ascetic) with the tip of a blade of Kusa grass, yet he is not worth the sixteenth particle of those who have well weighed the law.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: An evil deed, like newly-drawn milk, does not turn (suddenly); smouldering, like fire covered by ashes, it follows the fool.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: And when the evil deed, after it has become known, brings sorrow to the fool, then it destroys his bright lot, nay, it cleaves his head.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Let the fool wish for a false reputation, for precedence among the Bhikshus, for lordship in the convents, for worship among other people!
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: "May both the layman and he who has left the world think that this is done by me; may they be subject to me in everything which is to be done or is not to be done," thus is the mind of the fool, and his desire and pride increase.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: "One is the road that leads to wealth, another the road that leads to Nirvana;" if the Bhikshu, the disciple of Buddha, has learnt this, he will not yearn for honour, he will strive after separation from the world.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If you see an intelligent man who tells you where true treasures are to be found, who shows what is to be avoided, and administers reproofs, follow that wise man; it will be better, not worse, for those who follow him.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Let him admonish, let him teach, let him forbid what is improper!--he will be beloved of the good, by the bad he will be hated.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Do not have evil-doers for friends, do not have low people for friends: have virtuous people for friends, have for friends the best of men.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who drinks in the law lives happily with a serene mind: the sage rejoices always in the law, as preached by the elect (Ariyas).
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Well-makers lead the water (wherever they like); fletchers bend the arrow; carpenters bend a log of wood; wise people fashion themselves.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, wise people falter not amidst blame and praise.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Wise people, after they have listened to the laws, become serene, like a deep, smooth, and still lake.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Good people walk on whatever befall, the good do not prattle, longing for pleasure; whether touched by happiness or sorrow wise people never appear elated or depressed.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If, whether for his own sake, or for the sake of others, a man wishes neither for a son, nor for wealth, nor for lordship, and if he does not wish for his own success by unfair means, then he is good, wise, and virtuous.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Few are there among men who arrive at the other shore (become Arhats); the other people here run up and down the shore.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: But those who, when the law has been well preached to them, follow the law, will pass across the dominion of death, however difficult to overcome. 87, 88. A wise man should leave the dark state (of ordinary life), and follow the bright state (of the Bhikshu). After going from his home to a homeless state, he should in his retirement look for enjoyment where there seemed to be no enjoyment. Leaving all pleasures behind, and calling nothing his own, the wise man should purge himself from all the troubles of the mind.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Those whose mind is well grounded in the (seven) elements of knowledge, who without clinging to anything, rejoice in freedom from attachment, whose appetites have been conquered, and who are full of light, are free (even) in this world.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: There is no suffering for him who has finished his journey, and abandoned grief, who has freed himself on all sides, and thrown off all fetters.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: They depart with their thoughts well-collected, they are not happy in their abode; like swans who have left their lake, they leave their house and home.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Men who have no riches, who live on recognised food, who have perceived void and unconditioned freedom (Nirvana), their path is difficult to understand, like that of birds in the air.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He whose appetites are stilled, who is not absorbed in enjoyment, who has perceived void and unconditioned freedom (Nirvana), his path is difficult to understand, like that of birds in the air.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The gods even envy him whose senses, like horses well broken in by the driver, have been subdued, who is free from pride, and free from appetites.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Such a one who does his duty is tolerant like the earth, like Indra's bolt; he is like a lake without mud; no new births are in store for him.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: His thought is quiet, quiet are his word and deed, when he has obtained freedom by true knowledge, when he has thus become a quiet man.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The man who is free from credulity, but knows the uncreated, who has cut all ties, removed all temptations, renounced all desires, he is the greatest of men.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In a hamlet or in a forest, in the deep water or on the dry land, wherever venerable persons (Arhanta) dwell, that place is delightful.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Forests are delightful; where the world finds no delight, there the passionless will find delight, for they look not for pleasures.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Even though a speech be a thousand (of words), but made up of senseless words, one word of sense is better, which if a man hears, he becomes quiet.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Even though a Gatha (poem) be a thousand (of words), but made up of senseless words, one word of a Gatha is better, which if a man hears, he becomes quiet.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Though a man recite a hundred Gathas made up of senseless words, one word of the law is better, which if a man hears, he becomes quiet.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If one man conquer in battle a thousand times thousand men, and if another conquer himself, he is the greatest of conquerors. 104, 105. One's own self conquered is better than all other people; not even a god, a Gandharva, not Mara with Brahman could change into defeat the victory of a man who has vanquished himself, and always lives under restraint.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If a man for a hundred years sacrifice month after month with a thousand, and if he but for one moment pay homage to a man whose soul is grounded (in true knowledge), better is that homage than sacrifice for a hundred years.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Since He who is Infinite attained unto the Wisdom Supreme, the long, long ages of ten Kalpas have rolled away. The Light of His Dharma-Kaya is in this world eyes to the blind.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Seek refuge in the True Illumination! For the light of His Wisdom is infinite. In all the worlds there is nothing upon which His light shines not.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Take refuge in the Light universal. As the Light of His deliverance is boundless, he who is within it is freed from the lie of affirmation or denial.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Seek refuge in That which is beyond understanding, For His glory is all-embracing as the air. It shineth and pierceth all things, and there is nothing hid from the light thereof.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Take refuge in the ultimate Strength, for His pure radiance is above all things. He who perceiveth this Light is set free from the fetters of Karma.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Seek refuge in the World-Honoured. Since His glorious radiance is above all He is called the Buddha of Divine Light. And by Him is the darkness of the three worlds Enlightened.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Excellent is the Light of His Wisdom. Therefore is he called the Buddha of Clear Shining. He who is within the Light, being washed from the soil of Karma, shall attain unto the final deliverance.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Take refuge in the Mighty Consoler. Wheresoever His mercy shineth throughout all the worlds, men rejoice in its gladdening light.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The darkness of ignorance perisheth before His light. Therefore is He hailed as the Buddha of Radiant Wisdom. All the Buddhas and the threefold choir of sages praise Him.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: His glory shineth for ever and ever. Therefore is He called the Buddha of Everlasting Light. Most excellent is the virtue of this light, for he who perceiveth it is born into Paradise without dissolution of being.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The glory of the Infinite is boundless, therefore is He known as the Buddha of Light Past Comprehension. All the Buddhas glorify the majesty of His holiness that leadeth all the earth into His Kingdom.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: His clear shining transcendeth all revelation, nor can human speech utter it. Therefore is He named the Buddha of Light Unspeakable. All the Buddhas glorify the glory of the Infinite One who is Buddha through His promise of Light immeasurable.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Take refuge in Him who is Holiest of Holy. Sun and moon are lost in the ocean of His splendour. Therefore is He named that Infinite in whose radiance Sun and Moon are darkened. Before whose Divine Power even that Buddha made flesh in India himself faltereth in ascribing praise to the Majesty of His true glory.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Far beyond human numbering are the wise in the high assemblage of the Infinite One. Therefore let him who would be born into the Land of Purity seek refuge in the Great Congregation.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In Paradise are the Mighty unnumbered, Bodhisattvas ranked in that hierarchy nearest to the Perfect Enlightenment. Thence are they made flesh upon earth according to the way of salvation that all having life might be saved.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Take refuge in the ocean-deep Soul Universal. For the sake of all dwelling in the Ten Regions hath He kept the fullness of all the Teachings, in His divine and mighty promises.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who is Infinite never resteth, for together with the Bodhisattvas of Compassion and Pure Reason He laboureth, that the souls of them that duly receive Him may have salvation, enlightening them with the light of His mercy.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: When he who is born into the land of Pure Peace returneth again into this sinful world, even like unto that Buddha made flesh in India, he wearieth not in seeking the welfare of all men.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Seek refuge in the World-Honoured, for His Divine Power is Almighty and beyond man’s measure, being made perfect in inconceivable Holiness.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Srāvakas, the Bodhisattvas, the Heavenly Beings and Souls in Paradise, they in whom wisdom is made equal unto beauty, declare their attributes in order, according to their former birth.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Seek refuge in Him in whom all strengths are equal. Nought is there to compare with the excellent beauty of the Souls in Paradise, for their being is infinite as space, and far are they above celestials and mortal man.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Whoso would be born into Paradise shall in this life be made one with those men that return no more unto birth and death. In that Pure Land is none who hath stood among doubting men, and none also who hath trusted in his own deeds for Salvation. To this do all the Buddhas witness.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If all having life in the Ten Regions hear this Holiest Name of Him that is Infinite, and attain unto the true faith, they shall obtain joy and gladness.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: For when a man with joy accepteth the sacred vow of Him that is infinite who saith, “I will not attain unto perfect Enlightenment unless in Me shall all the world be made whole,” at that very time he shall assuredly be born into Paradise.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Seek refuge in the Almighty Spirit. By the divine might of His promise, by the Infinite One was Paradise created; yea, and the Souls of men that dwell therein. And there is nought that may compare with them.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Seek refuge in the unutterable Wisdom. Of His Land of Peace the half cannot be told. Even the word of the Buddha himself could not utter it.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Myriads of happy souls were born, are born and shall be born into that Land of Purity, not from this world alone, but from the hidden worlds also, and the Ten Regions.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: So soon as man heareth the holy name of the Infinite One and with great gladness praiseth him, he shall attain to the reward of the holy Treasury of Merit.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Go forward, O Valiant Souls, seeking the Law though all the worlds fall into flame and ruin, for ye shall have passed beyond birth and death!
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The innumerable Buddhas praise the triumphant divinity of the Bringer of Light. To Him do gather the myriad Bodhisattvas, unnumbered as the Sands of Ganges in worship from the Eastern world.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: As from the East, so gather also to the Infinite One the Bodhisattvas from the Nine Regions of the worlds. With Sacred Psalms the Gautama Buddha himself laudeth the boundless glory of the Infinite One.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Seek refuge in the World-Honoured. To Him do the myriad Buddhas of the ten Regions bring homage with songs and praises, that they may sow the seeds of merit.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Bring homage to the Hall of Great Teaching and to the living Bo tree that is in Paradise! Yet this land, glorious with the Holy Tree, radiant with the Hall of Great Teaching that shineth with the Seven Jewels, where innumerable souls hastening from all the ends of the Earth shall be born, is but the temporal Paradise.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In awful reverence seek refuge in the purity of Him that welcometh. For by His Divine Promise was this glorious land, great beyond human measurement, made to be.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Seek refuge in the wisdom inconceivable. For the perfection of His Virtue—that Virtue availing for all the world, and the perfect way by which He willeth that man shall take refuge in Him, are past all human speech or thought.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
theme_evidence: Văn bản tôn giáo/đạo đức cần giữ ngữ cảnh; không tự biến thành quy luật tâm lý hoặc cam kết kết quả.
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Take refuge in the wisdom that is most truly infinite. For He is faithful, having promised in His Divine Might, and on his perfect clear promise that cannot be shaken is the merciful way of salvation builded.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Seek refuge in the heavenly harmony. For the jewel groves and gem trees of Paradise give forth a sweet and most excellent melody in pure and ordered unison.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Seek refuge in the Divine Promise, the Treasury of Merit, For the seven jewel trees are fragrant in Paradise where the flowers, the fruits, the branches and the leaves thereof Cast back their radiance the one to the other.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Bring homage to the perfect Righteousness. As the pure wind blows over the trees glorious with jewels, It draweth from them a noble music with five-fold strains of harmony.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In all the world is no place hidden from the glory shed by hundreds of myriad rays from the heart of every flower of Paradise.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Like unto a golden mountain reflecting the myriad rays of these heavenly blossoms, so is the form of the Infinite One.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: From His Sacred Body, as from a well-spring, floweth this light over the Ten Regions of the world. By His Sacred teaching He leadeth all having life into the way of light.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Seek refuge in the Treasury of Righteousness. For in Paradise is that holy lake, with its waters of eightfold Virtue, all-glorious with the seven jewels. And all this is the inconceivable handiwork of Purity.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Seek refuge in the All-Honoured. For when sorrow and sighing are fled away, the Holy Land shall rejoice with joy and singing. Therefore is it called Paradise.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
theme_evidence: Văn bản tôn giáo/đạo đức cần giữ ngữ cảnh; không tự biến thành quy luật tâm lý hoặc cam kết kết quả.
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Buddhas of the Three Ages and the Ten Regions, they in whom the Dual Wisdom is perfect and their illumination entire, lead all the worlds marvellously into the way of Salvation, the Truth being their Vehicle.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
theme_evidence: Văn bản tôn giáo/đạo đức cần giữ ngữ cảnh; không tự biến thành quy luật tâm lý hoặc cam kết kết quả.
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He that seeketh refuge in the Kingdom of the Infinite One is a citizen of the Kingdom of every Buddha. Let him that is set free, with single heart give praises unto One Buddha, for in so doing he praiseth all.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The faithful believer at that moment when he rejoiceth in the sound of the name of the Infinite One hath revealed unto his very eyes the Buddha of Light.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Let him that hath faith praise the Virtue of the Divine Wisdom. Let him strive to declare it unto all men that he may offer his thankfulness for the grace of the Buddha.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
theme_evidence: Văn bản tôn giáo/đạo đức cần giữ ngữ cảnh; không tự biến thành quy luật tâm lý hoặc cam kết kết quả.
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Venerable Ananda, rising from his seat, and looking upwards to the World-Honoured Gautama Buddha, his eyes being opened, marvelled greatly, seeing the glory of his Lord so transfigured.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Venerable Ananda asked the Cause of that glory, for the Lord, shining in the Light that was hitherto unseen of the world, taught openly, for the first time, that Truth for which He came into the world.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In the meditation of the Great Calm the Buddha whose countenance is glorious, commendeth the most excellent wisdom of Ananda for that he asked the way of knowledge, desiring to be instructed.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: That Buddha that was made flesh in India was in this world manifested that he might preach the Divine Promise of Him who is Infinite. Hard is it to see the hidden blossom of the myriad-century-blooming Lotus, so hard also is it for a man’s understanding to receive the message of that Blessed One.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Ten Kalpas of Ages have rolled away since He who is Infinite attained unto the Wisdom, yet before the myriads of the Kalpas He _was_.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who is of the Light Ineffable, Holiest Refuge of men, ordaining that His saving grace should be made manifest, duly considered all the worlds of the Ten Regions, under the guidance of the holy Buddha of Loka-is-Vara-Raja.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Purity, Rejoicing, Wisdom, these three are the Supernal Essence of the light of the Infinite One that enlighteneth all things, communicating good to all the worlds of the Ten Regions.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Teaching all that have life in the Ten Regions, that they might, with sincerity, faith, and hope, be born again into Paradise, He set forth that promise infinite and divine—the true seed of birth within the Kingdom of Truth.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Whoso attaineth unto the True Faith is in unity with them that return no more to birth and death, for having thus attained, they pass onward into Nirvana, their lives being ended.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In His great compassion the Blessed One accomplished His infinite wisdom in His divine promise, ordaining that womanhood shall be raised into manhood.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Instructing all that have life in the Ten Regions how they should through sincerity, effort, and hope be born into the Temporal Paradise, He faithfully promiseth to manifest Himself unto the eyes of the dying, opening wide the gate of all righteousness before them.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: By the divine promise to the dying of His consoling presence our Lord instructeth men that they shall make to grow all righteousness revealed in the Sutra of Meditation upon the Buddha of Infinite Life.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: All righteous deeds done of men in true obedience to the holy Doctrine of Sincerity and right-doing, are but the seed of merit that shall be born within the Temporal Paradise.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Instructing All that have life in the Ten Regions how that they may through sincerity, merit, and hope be born into the Temporal Paradise, He promiseth that no man shall lose salvation, for He hath opened the Gate of Truth.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: By the Divine Promise of the final salvation hath our Lord instructed the men of the Single Vehicle to recite His Holy Name that is the Essence of all the merit revealed in the Lesser Sutra of the Buddha of Infinite Life.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He that reciteth the Holy name by his own effort and in the mind of meditation or of dispersing, being led by the virtue of the divine promise of final salvation, turneth naturally in at the Gate of Truth.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
theme_evidence: Văn bản tôn giáo/đạo đức cần giữ ngữ cảnh; không tự biến thành quy luật tâm lý hoặc cam kết kết quả.
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He that holds not the True Faith, even though he desire to be born into the Pure Paradise of Joy, must go unto his own place, and it shall be in the border of the Outermost Places, for this is the fruit of doubting the mystery of the Supreme Wisdom.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: That a man should be a Buddha, made manifest in this world, is a rare thing and difficult. So difficult is it also to hear the excellent doctrine of all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. In all the myriads of Kalpas such a way comes seldom.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Difficult is it for men to find a wise Teacher; so is it also for them to be instructed and to hear the Holy Law. More difficult still is it to receive the True Faith.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: More difficult is it for men to receive the Divine Promise made unto men than to receive all other teachings. The Lord Buddha teacheth that this is of all hard things most difficult and yet again more difficult.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The true Doctrine teacheth men that they may become Buddhas in reciting the Holy Name, and so therefore is it that all other faiths and moralities are but transitory doorways unto the Truth. Man comprehendeth not that Pure Land of Peace unless he holdeth fast the true Doctrine, casting aside that which is transitory.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Seek refuge in the Sole Vehicle of merciful promise. For the transitory teachings have let and hindered men in the Way of Enlightenment so that they must needs pass through the long weariness of births and deaths.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: That Lord that was made flesh in India, the Lord of great pity, showing unto Vaidehi, Queen of Magadha, the golden mirror created by his marvellous power, commanded her to choose the Land of Pure Joy among all the worlds therein appearing.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Binbisara, he who commanded that an ascetic should be slain before his pre-ordained time was come, by his own son was imprisoned in a seven-walled prison as the due recompense of his violence.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Ajāta-Šatru, prince and heir of Magadha, denouncing his mother as a traitor, with drawn sword ran furiously upon her.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Then said Jīvaka the minister and another with him: “This act is worthy only of an outcast. For the fame of our race unworthy art thou to dwell in the Palace.” And earnestly did they counsel him to change his evil purpose.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Laying his hand on his sword-hilt, Jīvaka, the minister, drew backwards a few steps, steadfastly regarding the prince, that he might avert this great sin. And so it was that the prince laid down his sword, and secluded his mother in a palace.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Certain is it that Ananda with Vaidehi, Devadatta and yet others, bearing their part in this great sorrow of the royal palace of Magadha, must needs so suffer that they might know the infinite pity of the Blessed One, that Lord who in this world made manifest the true teaching.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: And all these wise ones having so received instruction revealed unto us, who are of all evil-doers worst, the true way, the refuge of His divine promise that absolveth all the sins of men.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: For when the full time was come that by the will of our Lord and of Vaidehi the teaching of the Pure Land should be made known here on Earth, Ajāta-Šatru, her son, sinned this sin, Varshakara his minister bearing testimony against it.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It is needful that the heart of a man be opened unto the Faith universal which He who is Blessed hath shown us, forsaking the belief that his own works shall save him, for in every man the power to perform righteous deeds is differing.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Eternal Father is called the Buddha of Infinite Light, because very mightily He holdeth in safety all beings dwelling in the Ten Regions of the world who, by His merciful enlightenment, recite His Holy Name.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The myriad Buddhas, unnumbered as the sands of Ganges, counsel all having life to trust in the Supernal Virtue of the Holy Name, declaring that weighed against this even righteous deeds are the lesser good.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The innumerable Buddhas, countless as the sands of Ganges, are a testimony and a shield to all that have life in this sorrowful and sinful world, declaring unto them that teaching most high and difficult of acceptance, which is the true faith.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
