rows.text: Whoso attaineth unto a Soul clear and enduring as diamond shall testify unto his thankfulness for the limitless grace of the Blessed One, for even the testimony and the safeguarding that he hath of all the Buddhas proceed only from the fulfilment of His most merciful promise.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The innumerable Buddhas, countless as the sands of Ganges, guide into a sure trust in the Holy Name those sinful creatures and evil-hearted that wander in the darkness of this wicked world bearing the five signs of degeneration upon it.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Having great pity, our Eternal Father lighteneth the dark night of ignorance, manifesting Himself in that Land of Joy as the Buddha of Infinite Light which enlighteneth all the worlds with its immeasurable glory.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: That Lord most compassionate, the Buddha of immeasurable Light, He who had attained unto the Supreme Wisdom even before the myriads of Kalpas were, pitying them that know not, made himself manifest in the Palace of Kapila as the Lord Sakya-muni.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If a man had the duration of all the myriad Kalpas, had he innumerable tongues and each of these tongues innumerable voices, yet should he vainly essay the praises of that Blessed One.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Lord instructeth us that the way into Paradise is straight and easy. Therefore whoso receiveth not this Truth is, in verity, called a man that hath not eyes to see nor ears to hear.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The One true freedom is the Highest, and the Absolute is perfect freedom. And when we attain unto that freedom, for us shall desire and doubt vanish away.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: When every man is beloved of us, even as the son of our own body, there is the Universal Mind made perfect in us. And this shall be in Paradise.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who is in all things supreme, is Himself Nirvana, and Nirvana is that true light that abideth in the Land that is to come, but this world cannot know it.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Our Lord instructeth us that he who rejoiceth in his faith is, in so doing, in unity with the Highest. For true faith is the seed of light, and the seed of true light is in itself the potentiality of that which is Deity.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Whoso trusteth not in the Supreme Wisdom of the Enlightened One, clinging unto his own purblind knowledge, must suffer by fire for long Kalpas of ages.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He that hath unending pity, the Buddha of Infinite Life, hath given unto us in the Sutra of Golden Light a teaching concerning long life, that the way of long life and the welfare of the people might be made known unto them.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Dengyo-Daishi, he who taught the Tendai-shu in the mount of Hiye, hath compassionately instructed us that we should recite Namuamida-butsu, that Holiest Name, as a sure shield against the seven sorts of calamities.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Whoso reciteth the Holy Name, that is higher than all other virtues, shall be set free from the fetters of the past, the present, and the future.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: To him that reciteth the Holy Name shall be good unending even in this world, for the sin of his former births is vanquished and his youth set free from death.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: To him that reciteth the Holy Name, shall Brahma and Chakra the great king bring homage, and about him shall heavenly beings and benignant deities keep watch throughout the days and nights.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: That man that reciteth the Holy Name shall the four mighty Regents in Heaven guard through the days and nights against the disturbance of all evil spirits.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: To him that reciteth the Holy Name shall the Deity of the Earth bring homage, watching over him throughout the day and night, as the shadow follows its substance.
rows.author: Shinran Shōnin; translated by S. Yamabe and L. Adams Beck
rows.work: Buddhist Psalms translated from the Japanese of Shinran Shonin
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The most fruitful growth of Buddhism in the Far East has resulted in the development of Zen and Shin.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The vigour and vitality which Buddhism still has after more than two thousand years of history, will be realised when one comes in contact with these two branches of Buddhism.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The one appeals to the inmost religious consciousness of mankind, while the other touches the intellectual and practical aspects of the Oriental mind, which is more intuitive than discursive, more mystical than logical.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If Zen is the ultra “self-power” wing of Buddhism, Shin represents the other extreme wing known as the “other-power,” and these two extremes are synthesised in the enlightened Buddha-consciousness.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Since the publication of my short note on Zen Buddhism in the _Journal of the Pali Text Society_, 1907, nothing of importance has been published in English on the subject except Professor Kwaiten Nukariya’s _Religion of the Samurai_, 1913.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In fact, even in Japanese or Chinese, this branch of Buddhism has received very slight attention from modern writers of Buddhism.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: This is due to the peculiar difficulties which accompany the study of it.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The “Goroku”[f1][1] (sayings) is the only literary form in which Zen expresses itself; and to understand it requires some special practical training in Zen, for mere knowledge of the Chinese, classical and historical, is far from being enough; even with the masterly understanding of the philosophy of general Buddhism, Zen is found quite hard to fathom.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Some of such scholars sometimes try to explain the truth and development of Zen, but they sadly fail to do justice to the subject.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
theme_evidence: Lời dẫn, đề tặng, tự thuật hoặc lịch sử xuất bản; giữ ngữ cảnh, không coi là danh ngôn của tác phẩm.
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: On the other hand, the Zen masters so called are unable to present their understanding in the light of modern thought.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Their most intellectually-productive years are spent in the Meditation Hall, and when they successively graduate from it, they are looked up to as adepts thoroughly versed in the kō-ans.[2] So far so good; but, unfortunately from the scholarly point of view, they remain contented with this, and do not show any lively intellectual interest in the psychology and philosophy of Zen.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Thus Zen is left to lie quietly sealed up in the “Sayings” of the masters and in the technical study of the kō-ans; it is thus incapacitated to walk out of the seclusion of the cloisters.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Of course, great mistake it would be if one should ever take the notion even for a moment that Zen could be mastered from its philosophical presentation or its psychological description; but this ought not to mean that Zen is not to be intelligently approached or to be made somewhat accessible by our ordinary means of reasoning.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: I need not mention that my attempts in the following pages are anything but adequate for the rational treatment of the subject.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: But as a tentative experiment to present Zen from our common-sense point of view and as a direct lineage of Buddhist faith as first proclaimed or rather realised by the Buddha, I hope I have worked towards removing some of the difficulties usually besetting us in the mastery of Zen thought.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: How far I have succeeded or how utterly I have failed,—this is naturally for the reader to judge.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The book is a collection of the Essays originally published in _The Eastern Buddhist_ except one on the “History of Zen Buddhism” which was written specially for this volume; but all of them have been thoroughly revised and in some parts entirely re-written and new chapters added.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The book will be followed by a second series of Essays before long, in which some more of the important points in the constitution of Zen will be treated.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The publication of these Essays in bookform is principally due to the most liberal encouragement, both material and moral, of Mr Yakichi Ataka, of Osaka, who is an old friend of the author’s and who has not forgotten the pledge half-seriously and half-dreamily made in our youthful days.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The author also owes a great deal to his wife in the preparation and revision of the MS, without which the book would have shown many more imperfections than it does now in various ways.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Lastly, in sending this humble work, not written in the author’s native tongue, out to the world, he cannot help thinking of his late teacher in Zen, Soyen Shaku, of Engakuji, Kamakura, with regret that his life had not been spared for several years yet, not only for the sake of Japanese Buddhism but for many of his lamenting friends.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: This is the seventh autumn for the maple-trees to scatter their crimson leaves over his grave at Matsu-ga-oka.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Might his spirit not for once be awakened from deep meditation and criticise the book now before the reader!
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: History of Zen Buddhism in China, from Bodhi-dharma to the Sixth Patriarch (Hui-nêng) 149
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Zen in its essence is the art of seeing into the nature of one’s own being, and it points the way from bondage to freedom.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: By making us drink right from the fountain of life, it liberates us from all the yokes under which we finite beings are usually suffering in this world.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: We can say that Zen liberates all the energies properly and naturally stored in each of us, which are in ordinary circumstances cramped and distorted so that they find no adequate channel for activity.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: This body of ours is something like an electric battery in which a mysterious power latently lies.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: When this power is not properly brought into operation, it either grows mouldy and withers away or is warped and expresses itself abnormally.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It is the object of Zen, therefore, to save us from going crazy or being crippled.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: This is what I mean by freedom, giving free play to all the creative and benevolent impulses inherently lying in our hearts.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Generally, we are blind to this fact, that we are in possession of all the necessary faculties that will make us happy and loving towards one another.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Zen, therefore, wants us to open a “third eye,” as Buddhists call it, to the hitherto undreamed-of region shut away from us through our own ignorance.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: When the cloud of ignorance disappears, the infinity of the heavens is manifested where we see for the first time into the nature of our own being.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: We now know the signification of life, we know that it is not blind striving, nor is it a mere display of brutal forces, but that while we know not definitely what the ultimate purport of life is, there is something in it that makes us feel infinitely blessed in the living of it and remain quite contented with it in all its evolution, without raising questions or entertaining pessimistic doubts.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: When we are full of vitality and not yet awakened to the knowledge of life, we cannot comprehend the seriousness of all the conflicts involved in it which are apparently for the moment in a state of quiescence.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: But sooner or later the time will come when we have to face life squarely and solve its most perplexing and most pressing riddles.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Says Confucius, “At fifteen my mind was directed to study, and at thirty I knew where to stand.” This is one of the wisest sayings of the Chinese sage.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Psychologists will all agree to this statement of his; for, generally speaking, fifteen is about the age youth begins to look around seriously and inquire into the meaning of life.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: All the spiritual powers until now securely hidden in the subconscious part of the mind break out almost simultaneously.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: And when this breaking out is too precipitous and violent, the mind may lose its balance more or less permanently; in fact, so many cases of nervous prostration reported during adolescence are chiefly due to this loss of the mental equilibrium.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In most cases the effect is not very grave and the crisis may pass without leaving deep marks.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: But in some characters, either through their inherent tendencies or on account of the influence of environment upon their plastic constitution, the spiritual awakening stirs them up to the very depths of their personality.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: This is the time you will be asked to choose between the “Everlasting No” and the “Everlasting Yea.” This choosing is what Confucius means by “study,” it is not studying the classics, but deeply delving into the mysteries of life.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Normally, the outcome of the struggle is the “Everlasting Yea,” or “Let thy will be done”; for life is after all a form of affirmation however negatively it might be conceived by the pessimists.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: But we cannot deny the fact that there are many things in this world which will turn our too sensitive minds towards the other direction and make us exclaim with Andreyev in “The Life of Man”: “I curse everything that you have given.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: With my last thought I will shout into your asinine ears: Be accursed, be accursed!” This is a terrible indictment of life, it is a complete negation of life, it is a most dismal picture of the destiny of man on earth.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: “Leaving no trace” is quite true, for we know nothing of our future except that we all pass away including the very earth from which we have come.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: As long as life is a form of struggle, it cannot be anything but pain.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Does not a struggle mean the impact of two conflicting forces, each trying to get the upperhand of the other?
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If the battle is lost, the outcome is death, and death is the fearsomest thing in the world.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Even when death is conquered, one is left alone, and the loneliness is sometimes more unbearable than the struggle itself.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: One may not be conscious of all this, and may go on indulging in those momentary pleasures that are afforded by the senses.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: But this being unconscious does not in the least alter the facts of life.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: However insistently the blind may deny the existence of the sun, they cannot annihilate it.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The tropical heat will mercilessly scorch them, and if they do not take proper care, they will all be wiped away from the surface of the earth.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Buddha was perfectly right when he propounded his “Fourfold Noble Truth” the first of which is that life is pain.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Did not everyone of us come to this world screaming and in a way protesting?
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: To come out into cold and prohibitive surroundings after a soft, warm motherly womb was surely a painful incident to say the least.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Puberty is usually accompanied with a mental as well as a physical disturbance.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The growth of the organism called society is also marked with painful cataclysms, and we are at present witnessing one of its birth-throes.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: We may calmly reason and say that this is all inevitable, that inasmuch as every reconstruction means the destruction of the old regime, we cannot help going through a painful operation.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: But this cold intellectual analysis does not alleviate whatever harrowing feelings we have to undergo.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: For the more you suffer the deeper grows your character, and with the deepening of your character you read the more penetratingly into the secrets of life.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: All great artists, all great religious leaders, and all great social reformers have come out of the intensest struggles which they fought bravely, quite frequently in tears and with bleeding hearts.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Mencius is right when he says that when Heaven wants to perfect a great man it tries him in every possible way until he comes out triumphantly from all his painful experiences.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: To me Oscar Wilde seems always posing or striving for an effect; he may be a great artist, but there is something in him that turns me away from him.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Yet he exclaims in his _De Profundis_: “During the last few months I have, after terrible difficulties and struggles, been able to comprehend some of the lessons hidden in the heart of pain.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Clergymen and people who use phrases without wisdom sometimes talk of suffering as a mystery.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: One approaches the whole of history from a different standpoint.” You will observe here what sanctifying effects his prison life produced on his character.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If he had had to go through a similar trial in the beginning of his career, he might have been able to produce far greater works than those we have of him at present.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: We seem to carry it all the time from childhood up to the time we finally pass away.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: We are, however, given many chances to break through this shell, and the first and greatest of them is when we reach adolescence.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: This is the first time the ego really comes to recognise the “other.” I mean the awakening of sexual love.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: An ego, entire and undivided, now begins to feel a sort of split in itself.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Love hitherto dormant deep in his heart lifts its head and causes a great commotion in it.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: For the love now stirred demands at once the assertion of the ego and its annihilation.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Love makes the ego lose itself in the object it loves, and yet at the same time it wants to have the object as its own.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: This elemental feeling must be one of the divine agencies whereby man is urged to advance in his upward walk.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The greatest bulk of literature ever produced in this world is but the harping on the same string of love, and we never seem to grow weary of it.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: What I want to emphasise in this connection is this, that through the awakening of love we get a glimpse into the infinity of things, and that this glimpse urges youth to Romanticism or to Rationalism according to his temperament and environment and education.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: When the ego-shell is broken and the “other” is taken into its own body, we can say that the ego has denied itself or that the ego has taken its first steps towards the infinite.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Religiously, here ensues an intense struggle between the finite and the infinite, between the intellect and a higher power, or, more plainly, between the flesh and the spirit.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: This is the problem of problems that has driven many a youth into the hands of Satan.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: When a grown-up man looks back to these youthful days, he cannot but feel a sort of shudder going through his entire frame.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The struggle to be fought in sincerity may go on up to the age of thirty when Confucius states that he knew where to stand.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The religious consciousness is now fully awakened, and all the possible ways of escaping from the struggle or bringing it to an end are most earnestly sought in every direction.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Books are read, lectures are attended, sermons are greedily taken in, and various religious exercises or disciplines are tried.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In the first place, Zen proposes its solution by directly appealing to facts of personal experience and not to book-knowledge.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
theme_evidence: Đã đọc toàn văn dòng; chủ đề xét theo ý chính, chưa xác minh nguồn/quyền để Release.
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The nature of one’s own being where apparently rages the struggle between the finite and the infinite is to be grasped by a higher faculty than the intellect.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: For Zen says it is the latter that first made us raise the question which it could not answer by itself, and that therefore it is to be put aside to make room for something higher and more enlightening.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Though it raises questions enough to disturb the serenity of the mind, it is too frequently unable to give satisfactory answers to them.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It upsets the blissful peace of ignorance and yet it does not restore the former state of things by offering something else.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Because it points out ignorance, it is often considered illuminating, whereas the fact is that it disturbs, not necessarily always bringing light on its path.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It is not final, it waits for something higher than itself for the solution of all the questions it will raise regardless of consequences.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If it were able to bring a new order into the disturbance and settle it once for all, there would have been no need for philosophy after it had been first systematised by a great thinker, by an Aristotle, or by a Hegel.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: But the history of thought proves that each new structure raised by a man of extraordinary intellect is sure to be pulled down by the succeeding ones.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: This constant pulling down and building up is all right as far as philosophy itself is concerned; for the inherent nature of the intellect, as I take it, demands it and we cannot put a stop to the progress of philosophical inquiries any more than to our breathing.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: But when it comes to the question of life itself we cannot wait for the ultimate solution to be offered by the intellect even if it could do so.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: We cannot suspend even for a moment our life-activity for philosophy to unravel its mysteries.
rows.author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Books on the Far East often mention a sect of Buddhism called Zen.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: They say that it was a “school of abstract meditation” and that it exercised a profound influence upon art and literature; but they tell us very little about what Zen actually was, about its relation to ordinary Buddhism, its history, or the exact nature of its influence upon the arts.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The reason of this is that very little of the native literature which deals with Zen has yet been translated, perhaps because it is written in early Chinese colloquial, a language the study of which has been almost wholly neglected by Europeans and also (to judge by some of their attempts to translate it) by the Japanese themselves.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The present paper makes no attempt at profundity, but it is based on the study of original texts and furnishes, I hope, some information not hitherto accessible.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Before describing the origins of Zen itself I must give some general account of Buddhism.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: At the time when it reached China[1] there were two kinds of Buddhism, called the Lesser Vehicle and the Greater.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The former, Primitive Buddhism, possessed scriptures which in part at any rate were genuine; that is to say, they recorded words actually used by Shākyamuni.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The ordinary adherent of this religion did not hope to become a Buddha; Buddhas indeed were regarded as extremely rare.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He only aspired to become an Arhat, that is “an ascetic ripe for annihilation,” one who is about to escape from the wheel of reincarnation--whose present incarnation is an antechamber to Nirvāna.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: To such aspirants the Buddha gives no assistance; he is what children in their games call “home,” and his followers must pant after him as best they can.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Those who found this religion too comfortless invented another, which became known as Mahāyāna, the Greater Vehicle.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Putting their doctrines into the mouth of Shākyamuni, they fabricated _ad hoc_ sermons of enormous length, preached (so they asserted) by the Buddha himself in his “second period” to those who were ripe to receive the whole truth.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The great feature of this new Buddhism was the intervention of the merciful Bodhisattvas, _illuminati_ who, though fit for Buddhahood, voluntarily renounced it in order to help mankind.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The first Buddhist books to reach China emanated from the Lesser Vehicle.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: But the Greater Vehicle or Bodhisattva-Buddhism soon prevailed, and by the sixth century A.D. over two thousand works, most of them belonging to the Greater Vehicle, had been translated into Chinese.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: There were already many sects in China, the chief of which were:
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: This was the form of Buddhism which appealed to the uneducated.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It taught that a Buddha named Amida presides over the Western Paradise, where he will receive the souls of those that worship him.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The conception of this Paradise closely resembles the Christian idea of Heaven and may have been derived from it.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: (2) The _Tendai_ Sect, founded at the end of the sixth century.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Its teaching was based on a scripture of enormous length called the _Saddharma Pundarīka Sūtra_, which is translated by Kern in the Sacred Books of the East.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In the year 520 A.D. there arrived at Canton a missionary from Southern India.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: His name was Bodhidharma and he appears to have been the younger son of an Indian Prince.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The reigning Emperor of China was a munificent patron of Buddhism.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He had built monasteries, given alms, distributed scriptures, defended the faith.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Hearing that a Buddhist prince had arrived from India he summoned him at once to his Capital.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The following conversation took place in the Palace at Nanking:
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: _Emperor_: You will be interested to hear that I have built many monasteries, distributed scriptures, given alms, and upheld the Faith.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: _Bodhidharma_: In the obliteration of Matter through Absolute Knowledge, not by external acts.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: _Emperor_: Which is the Divine and Primal Aspect of Reality?
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Monasticism, a huge vested interest, decried him, and after a short stay in Nanking he started northward, towards the Capital of the Wei Tartars, who then ruled over a large part of China.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Wei Emperor, like his Chinese confrère, was also a great patron of Buddhism, and he, too, desired an interview with the Indian priest.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: But Bodhidharma had done with Emperors, and settled in a small country temple, where he lived till his death nine years later.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Some say that he tried to visit the Capital of the Weis, but was prevented by the intrigues of the monks there.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He left behind him a few short tractates, the substance of which is as follows:
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Buddha is simply a Sanskrit word meaning “initiate.” The Absolute is immanent in every man’s heart.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: This “treasure of the heart” is the only Buddha that exists.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Prayer, scripture-reading, fasting, the observance of monastic rules--all are useless.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: You may know by heart all the Sūtras of the twelve divisions, and yet be unable to escape from the Wheel of Life and Death.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: One thing alone avails--to discover the unreality of the World by contemplating the Absolute which is at the root of one’s own nature.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Some one asked him: “Why may we not worship the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas?” He answered:
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: “Ogres and hobgoblins can at will assume the outward form of Bodhisattvas; such are heretical and not of the true Buddha.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The highest truths cannot be written down or taught by speech.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: A man who cannot write a word, can yet contemplate his own heart and become wise.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Knowledge of 1,000 Sūtras and 10,000 Shāstras cannot help him to realise the Absolute within him.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He was asked: “Can a layman with wife and children, one given over to the lusts of the flesh, achieve Buddhahood?” He answered:
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: “Provided he contemplate his own inner-nature, he will achieve Buddhahood.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Even a butcher can achieve Buddhahood, if he searches in his own heart.”
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: “What,” cried his listeners, “a butcher, who lives by taking life, and _he_ achieve Buddhahood?” The master replied:
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: “I have come from India only to teach you that Buddha is Thought.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: As for walking on water or through fire, climbing sword-wheels, fasting, sitting upright for hours without rest--all such practices are heretical; they belong to the World of Being.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Expanding, it covers the whole world; shrinking, it is too small to lodge a pin.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: For I have learnt to know that the outer world is empty and untenanted.”
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The terms “thought,” “Buddha,” etc., used by Bodhidharma correspond exactly to the _brahman_ of the Upanishads.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Mystic contemplation or _yoga_ had been used by the Brahmins and was not unknown to the early Buddhists.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: But Bodhidharma was the first to insist upon it as the sole means of salvation.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: derived from the Nihilistic School of Nāgārjuna (1st century
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Yet though his whole teaching turned on this “meditation” or “Zen,” he left behind him no exact directions for the practice of it.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Having shown the end, he left it to each individual to find his own means.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Rules, dogmas and definitions were precisely what he set out to destroy.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Less than a hundred years after his death another Indian, Buddhapriya, came to China and there defined with exactitude and blunt materiality the various forms of meditation.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The transition from the spirituality of Bodhidharma to the grossness of his follower is, however, typical of religious history.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The poetry of Christ turns into the theology of Paul; the hovel of Saint Francis into the mansion of Brother Elias.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He first describes the different attitudes in which Zen may be practised, with an exact account of the correct position for hands, feet, head, etc.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The normal attitude of meditation, cross-legged, with upright back and hands locked over the knees is familiar to every one.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Zen could also be practised while walking and, in cases of sickness, while lying down.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Buddhapriya’s instructions are in the form of question and answer.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: _Question._--How does the Zen practised by heretics and by the other schools of Buddhism differ from our Zen?
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Zen of the Greater Vehicle only abstracts man and phenomena.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: _Answer._--First put far away from you all anger and malice, and fill your heart with kindness and compassion.
rows.author: Arthur Waley

rows.text: _Question._--Can the beginner at once proceed to the contemplation of non-Being?
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: I have never yet seen one who straightway achieved the vision of non-Reality.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If for example he were meditating in this room he must first banish from his mind every part of the world except the city of Ch’ang-an.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Next, every room in the monastery except this cell, every object but himself, every part of himself except the end of his nose.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Finally the end of his nose hangs in space like a drop of dew and on this nose-end he concentrates his mind.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: For example--persuade yourself that your navel is a minute rivulet running through the sands.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: When this conception is firmly achieved, you will see a bright light and ultimately, the body growing transparent, you will behold the working of your bowels.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Or again, regard your head as the top of a hollow pipe which runs straight down through your body into the earth.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Meditate upon the top of your head, that is to say, upon the mouth of the drain-pipe, and then gradually ascend in your thoughts to a height of four inches above the head, and concentrate firmly on this conception.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
theme_evidence: Văn bản tôn giáo/đạo đức cần giữ ngữ cảnh; không tự biến thành quy luật tâm lý hoặc cam kết kết quả.
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: You will thus easily pass into the contemplation of non-Being, having performed the transition from elementary to complete Zen as comfortably as a workman climbs the rungs of a ladder.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: _Question._--Are there any signs whereby I may know that I have attained to Samādhi?[4]
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Sometimes you will feel a sensation as of bugs or ants creeping over your skin; or again, it will appear to you that a cloud or mass of white cotton-wool is rising immediately behind your back.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In neither case must you be discomposed or put out your hand.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Sometimes it will seem as though oil were dripping down from your head and face; sometimes a light will shine from out of the ground you are sitting upon.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Sometimes when you have been sitting for a long while and your back is aching, you will suddenly hear a sound of rapping with the fingers or a noise as of some one bumping against the door.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: These are the Good Spirits of Heaven, come to warn you against sleep.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Again, it may happen that you have an agreeable sense of lightness and floating; this is a good sign.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Beware, however, of a _painful_ sense of lightness; for this may merely indicate flatulence.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: A light filling the whole room is a premonitory sign of Zen; to smell strange fragrances not known on earth is a sign of whole and utter Abstraction.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The practicant must not heed them; for if by them he be encouraged or dismayed, all his work will be undone.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Zen should be practised in a quiet room or under a tree or among tombs or sitting on the dewy earth.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: _Answer._--To be sure it may; but each must face his neighbour’s back.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: When there are many sitting together at night, a lamp or candle may be lit; but when there are few together, it ought not to be used.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: _Question._--Need I wear monastic vestments at my meditations?
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Why, you need wear no clothes at all, if so be you are alone.
