rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Zen was at first a purely personal discipline, non-monastic, non-ethical, not demanding the acceptance of any Scripture or any tradition.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In modern Japan it has to some extent regained this character.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In China the habit of quoting written authority was too strong to be easily discarded.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Zen masters soon began to answer difficult questions by quoting from the Buddhist Scriptures.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Convenience dictated that practicants of Zen should live in communities and monasticism was soon established in their sect, as in every other sect of Buddhism.
rows.author: Arthur Waley
rows.work: Zen Buddhism, and Its Relation to Art
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If a man for a hundred years worship Agni (fire) in the forest, and if he but for one moment pay homage to a man whose soul is grounded (in true knowledge), better is that homage than sacrifice for a hundred years.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Whatever a man sacrifice in this world as an offering or as an oblation for a whole year in order to gain merit, the whole of it is not worth a quarter (a farthing); reverence shown to the righteous is better.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who always greets and constantly reveres the aged, four things will increase to him, viz. life, beauty, happiness, power.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: But he who lives a hundred years, vicious and unrestrained, a life of one day is better if a man is virtuous and reflecting.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: And he who lives a hundred years, ignorant and unrestrained, a life of one day is better if a man is wise and reflecting.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: And he who lives a hundred years, idle and weak, a life of one day is better if a man has attained firm strength.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: And he who lives a hundred years, not seeing beginning and end, a life of one day is better if a man sees beginning and end.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: And he who lives a hundred years, not seeing the immortal place, a life of one day is better if a man sees the immortal place.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: And he who lives a hundred years, not seeing the highest law, a life of one day is better if a man sees the highest law.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If a man would hasten towards the good, he should keep his thought away from evil; if a man does what is good slothfully, his mind delights in evil.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If a man commits a sin, let him not do it again; let him not delight in sin: pain is the outcome of evil.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If a man does what is good, let him do it again; let him delight in it: happiness is the outcome of good.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Even an evil-doer sees happiness as long as his evil deed has not ripened; but when his evil deed has ripened, then does the evil-doer see evil.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Even a good man sees evil days, as long as his good deed has not ripened; but when his good deed has ripened, then does the good man see happy days.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Let no man think lightly of evil, saying in his heart, It will not come nigh unto me. Even by the falling of water-drops a water-pot is filled; the fool becomes full of evil, even if he gather it little by little.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Let no man think lightly of good, saying in his heart, It will not come nigh unto me. Even by the falling of water-drops a water-pot is filled; the wise man becomes full of good, even if he gather it little by little.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Let a man avoid evil deeds, as a merchant, if he has few companions and carries much wealth, avoids a dangerous road; as a man who loves life avoids poison.

theme_evidence: Văn bản tôn giáo/đạo đức cần giữ ngữ cảnh; không tự biến thành quy luật tâm lý hoặc cam kết kết quả.
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who has no wound on his hand, may touch poison with his hand; poison does not affect one who has no wound; nor is there evil for one who does not commit evil.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If a man offend a harmless, pure, and innocent person, the evil falls back upon that fool, like light dust thrown up against the wind.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Some people are born again; evil-doers go to hell; righteous people go to heaven; those who are free from all worldly desires attain Nirvana.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Not in the sky, not in the midst of the sea, not if we enter into the clefts of the mountains, is there known a spot in the whole world where a man might be freed from an evil deed.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Not in the sky, not in the midst of the sea, not if we enter into the clefts of the mountains, is there known a spot in the whole world where death could not overcome (the mortal).
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
theme_evidence: Văn bản tôn giáo/đạo đức cần giữ ngữ cảnh; không tự biến thành quy luật tâm lý hoặc cam kết kết quả.
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: All men tremble at punishment, all men fear death; remember that you are like unto them, and do not kill, nor cause slaughter.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: All men tremble at punishment, all men love life; remember that thou art like unto them, and do not kill, nor cause slaughter.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who seeking his own happiness punishes or kills beings who also long for happiness, will not find happiness after death.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who seeking his own happiness does not punish or kill beings who also long for happiness, will find happiness after death.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Do not speak harshly to anybody; those who are spoken to will answer thee in the same way. Angry speech is painful, blows for blows will touch thee.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If, like a shattered metal plate (gong), thou utter not, then thou hast reached Nirvana; contention is not known to thee.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: As a cowherd with his staff drives his cows into the stable, so do Age and Death drive the life of men.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: A fool does not know when he commits his evil deeds: but the wicked man burns by his own deeds, as if burnt by fire.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who inflicts pain on innocent and harmless persons, will soon come to one of these ten states:
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He will have cruel suffering, loss, injury of the body, heavy affliction, or loss of mind,
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Or a misfortune coming from the king, or a fearful accusation, or loss of relations, or destruction of treasures,
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Or lightning-fire will burn his houses; and when his body is destroyed, the fool will go to hell.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Not nakedness, not platted hair, not dirt, not fasting, or lying on the earth, not rubbing with dust, not sitting motionless, can purify a mortal who has not overcome desires.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who, though dressed in fine apparel, exercises tranquillity, is quiet, subdued, restrained, chaste, and has ceased to find fault with all other beings, he indeed is a Brahmana, an ascetic (sramana), a friar (bhikshu).
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Is there in this world any man so restrained by humility that he does not mind reproof, as a well-trained horse the whip?
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Like a well-trained horse when touched by the whip, be ye active and lively, and by faith, by virtue, by energy, by meditation, by discernment of the law you will overcome this great pain (of reproof), perfect in knowledge and in behaviour, and never forgetful.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Well-makers lead the water (wherever they like); fletchers bend the arrow; carpenters bend a log of wood; good people fashion themselves.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: How is there laughter, how is there joy, as this world is always burning? Why do you not seek a light, ye who are surrounded by darkness?
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Look at this dressed-up lump, covered with wounds, joined together, sickly, full of many thoughts, which has no strength, no hold!
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: This body is wasted, full of sickness, and frail; this heap of corruption breaks to pieces, life indeed ends in death.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Those white bones, like gourds thrown away in the autumn, what pleasure is there in looking at them?
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: After a stronghold has been made of the bones, it is covered with flesh and blood, and there dwell in it old age and death, pride and deceit.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The brilliant chariots of kings are destroyed, the body also approaches destruction, but the virtue of good people never approaches destruction,--thus do the good say to the good.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: A man who has learnt little, grows old like an ox; his flesh grows, but his knowledge does not grow. 153, 154. Looking for the maker of this tabernacle, I shall have to run through a course of many births, so long as I do not find (him); and painful is birth again and again. But now, maker of the tabernacle, thou hast been seen; thou shalt not make up this tabernacle again. All thy rafters are broken, thy ridge-pole is sundered; the mind, approaching the Eternal (visankhara, nirvana), has attained to the extinction of all desires.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
theme_evidence: Capture gộp nhiều kệ; phải tách theo locator trước khi dịch và chọn chủ đề.
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Men who have not observed proper discipline, and have not gained treasure in their youth, perish like old herons in a lake without fish.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Men who have not observed proper discipline, and have not gained treasure in their youth, lie, like broken bows, sighing after the past.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If a man hold himself dear, let him watch himself carefully; during one at least out of the three watches a wise man should be watchful.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Let each man direct himself first to what is proper, then let him teach others; thus a wise man will not suffer.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If a man make himself as he teaches others to be, then, being himself well subdued, he may subdue (others); one's own self is indeed difficult to subdue.

rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Self is the lord of self, who else could be the lord? With self well subdued, a man finds a lord such as few can find.

rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The evil done by oneself, self-begotten, self-bred, crushes the foolish, as a diamond breaks a precious stone.

rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He whose wickedness is very great brings himself down to that state where his enemy wishes him to be, as a creeper does with the tree which it surrounds.

rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Bad deeds, and deeds hurtful to ourselves, are easy to do; what is beneficial and good, that is very difficult to do.

rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The foolish man who scorns the rule of the venerable (Arahat), of the elect (Ariya), of the virtuous, and follows false doctrine, he bears fruit to his own destruction, like the fruits of the Katthaka reed.

rows.text: By oneself the evil is done, by oneself one suffers; by oneself evil is left undone, by oneself one is purified. Purity and impurity belong to oneself, no one can purify another.

rows.text: Not to blame, not to strike, to live restrained under the law, to be moderate in eating, to sleep and sit alone, and to dwell on the highest thoughts,--this is the teaching of the Awakened.

rows.text: A supernatural person (a Buddha) is not easily found, he is not born everywhere. Wherever such a sage is born, that race prospers.

rows.text: Happy is the arising of the awakened, happy is the teaching of the True Law, happy is peace in the church, happy is the devotion of those who are at peace. 195, 196. He who pays homage to those who deserve homage, whether the awakened (Buddha) or their disciples, those who have overcome the host (of evils), and crossed the flood of sorrow, he who pays homage to such as have found deliverance and know no fear, his merit can never be measured by anybody.

rows.text: Let us live happily then, not hating those who hate us! among men who hate us let us dwell free from hatred!

rows.text: This is an old saying, O Atula, this is not only of to-day: `They blame him who sits silent, they blame him who speaks much, they also blame him who says little; there is no one on earth who is not blamed.'

rows.text: Make thyself an island, work hard, be wise! When thy impurities are blown away, and thou art free from guilt, thou wilt not enter again into birth and decay.

rows.text: There is no fire like passion, there is no shark like hatred, there is no snare like folly, there is no torrent like greed.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The fault of others is easily perceived, but that of oneself is difficult to perceive; a man winnows his neighbour's faults like chaff, but his own fault he hides, as a cheat hides the bad die from the gambler.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If a man looks after the faults of others, and is always inclined to be offended, his own passions will grow, and he is far from the destruction of passions.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: There is no path through the air, a man is not a Samana by outward acts. The world delights in vanity, the Tathagatas (the Buddhas) are free from vanity.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: There is no path through the air, a man is not a Samana by outward acts. No creatures are eternal; but the awakened (Buddha) are never shaken.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: A man is not learned because he talks much; he who is patient, free from hatred and fear, he is called learned.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
theme_evidence: Văn bản tôn giáo/đạo đức cần giữ ngữ cảnh; không tự biến thành quy luật tâm lý hoặc cam kết kết quả.
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: A man is not a supporter of the law because he talks much; even if a man has learnt little, but sees the law bodily, he is a supporter of the law, a man who never neglects the law.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: A man is not an elder because his head is grey; his age may be ripe, but he is called `Old-in-vain.'
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He in whom there is truth, virtue, love, restraint, moderation, he who is free from impurity and is wise, he is called an elder.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
theme_evidence: Văn bản tôn giáo/đạo đức cần giữ ngữ cảnh; không tự biến thành quy luật tâm lý hoặc cam kết kết quả.
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: An envious greedy, dishonest man does not become respectable by means of much talking only, or by the beauty of his complexion.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He in whom all this is destroyed, and taken out with the very root, he, when freed from hatred and wise, is called respectable.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Not by tonsure does an undisciplined man who speaks falsehood become a Samana; can a man be a Samana who is still held captive by desire and greediness?
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who always quiets the evil, whether small or large, he is called a Samana (a quiet man), because he has quieted all evil.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: A man is not a mendicant (Bhikshu) simply because he asks others for alms; he who adopts the whole law is a Bhikshu, not he who only begs.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who is above good and evil, who is chaste, who with knowledge passes through the world, he indeed is called a Bhikshu. 268, 269. A man is not a Muni because he observes silence (mona, i.e. mauna), if he is foolish and ignorant; but the wise who, taking the balance, chooses the good and avoids evil, he is a Muni, and is a Muni thereby; he who in this world weighs both sides is called a Muni.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: A man is not an elect (Ariya) because he injures living creatures; because he has pity on all living creatures, therefore is a man called Ariya. 271, 272. Not only by discipline and vows, not only by much learning, not by entering into a trance, not by sleeping alone, do I earn the happiness of release which no worldling can know. Bhikshu, be not confident as long as thou hast not attained the extinction of desires.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The best of ways is the eightfold; the best of truths the four words; the best of virtues passionlessness; the best of men he who has eyes to see.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
theme_evidence: Văn bản tôn giáo/đạo đức cần giữ ngữ cảnh; không tự biến thành quy luật tâm lý hoặc cam kết kết quả.
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: This is the way, there is no other that leads to the purifying of intelligence. Go on this way! Everything else is the deceit of Mara (the tempter).
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If you go on this way, you will make an end of pain! The way was preached by me, when I had understood the removal of the thorns (in the flesh).
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: You yourself must make an effort. The Tathagatas (Buddhas) are only preachers. The thoughtful who enter the way are freed from the bondage of Mara.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: `All created things perish,' he who knows and sees this becomes passive in pain; this is the way to purity.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: `All created things are grief and pain,' he who knows and sees this becomes passive in pain; this is the way that leads to purity.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: `All forms are unreal,' he who knows and sees this becomes passive in pain; this is the way that leads to purity.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who does not rouse himself when it is time to rise, who, though young and strong, is full of sloth, whose will and thought are weak, that lazy and idle man will never find the way to knowledge.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Watching his speech, well restrained in mind, let a man never commit any wrong with his body! Let a man but keep these three roads of action clear, and he will achieve the way which is taught by the wise.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Through zeal knowledge is gotten, through lack of zeal knowledge is lost; let a man who knows this double path of gain and loss thus place himself that knowledge may grow.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Cut down the whole forest (of lust), not a tree only! Danger comes out of the forest (of lust). When you have cut down both the forest (of lust) and its undergrowth, then, Bhikshus, you will be rid of the forest and free!
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: So long as the love of man towards women, even the smallest, is not destroyed, so long is his mind in bondage, as the calf that drinks milk is to its mother.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Cut out the love of self, like an autumn lotus, with thy hand! Cherish the road of peace. Nirvana has been shown by Sugata (Buddha).
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: `Here I shall dwell in the rain, here in winter and summer,' thus the fool meditates, and does not think of his death.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Death comes and carries off that man, praised for his children and flocks, his mind distracted, as a flood carries off a sleeping village.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Sons are no help, nor a father, nor relations; there is no help from kinsfolk for one whom death has seized.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: A wise and good man who knows the meaning of this, should quickly clear the way that leads to Nirvana.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If by leaving a small pleasure one sees a great pleasure, let a wise man leave the small pleasure, and look to the great.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who, by causing pain to others, wishes to obtain pleasure for himself, he, entangled in the bonds of hatred, will never be free from hatred.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: What ought to be done is neglected, what ought not to be done is done; the desires of unruly, thoughtless people are always increasing.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: But they whose whole watchfulness is always directed to their body, who do not follow what ought not to be done, and who steadfastly do what ought to be done, the desires of such watchful and wise people will come to an end.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: A true Brahmana goes scatheless, though he have killed father and mother, and two valiant kings, though he has destroyed a kingdom with all its subjects.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: A true Brahmana goes scatheless, though he have killed father and mother, and two holy kings, and an eminent man besides.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The disciples of Gotama (Buddha) are always well awake, and their thoughts day and night are always set on Buddha.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The disciples of Gotama are always well awake, and their thoughts day and night are always set on the law.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The disciples of Gotama are always well awake, and their thoughts day and night are always set on the church.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The disciples of Gotama are always well awake, and their thoughts day and night are always set on their body.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The disciples of Gotama are always well awake, and their mind day and night always delights in compassion.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The disciples of Gotama are always well awake, and their mind day and night always delights in meditation.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It is hard to leave the world (to become a friar), it is hard to enjoy the world; hard is the monastery, painful are the houses; painful it is to dwell with equals (to share everything in common) and the itinerant mendicant is beset with pain. Therefore let no man be an itinerant mendicant and he will not be beset with pain.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Whatever place a faithful, virtuous, celebrated, and wealthy man chooses, there he is respected.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Good people shine from afar, like the snowy mountains; bad people are not seen, like arrows shot by night.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He alone who, without ceasing, practises the duty of sitting alone and sleeping alone, he, subduing himself, will rejoice in the destruction of all desires alone, as if living in a forest.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who says what is not, goes to hell; he also who, having done a thing, says I have not done it. After death both are equal, they are men with evil deeds in the next world.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Many men whose shoulders are covered with the yellow gown are ill-conditioned and unrestrained; such evil-doers by their evil deeds go to hell.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Better it would be to swallow a heated iron ball, like flaring fire, than that a bad unrestrained fellow should live on the charity of the land.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Four things does a wreckless man gain who covets his neighbour's wife,--a bad reputation, an uncomfortable bed, thirdly, punishment, and lastly, hell.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: There is bad reputation, and the evil way (to hell), there is the short pleasure of the frightened in the arms of the frightened, and the king imposes heavy punishment; therefore let no man think of his neighbour's wife.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: As a grass-blade, if badly grasped, cuts the arm, badly-practised asceticism leads to hell.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: An act carelessly performed, a broken vow, and hesitating obedience to discipline, all this brings no great reward.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If anything is to be done, let a man do it, let him attack it vigorously! A careless pilgrim only scatters the dust of his passions more widely.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: An evil deed is better left undone, for a man repents of it afterwards; a good deed is better done, for having done it, one does not repent.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Like a well-guarded frontier fort, with defences within and without, so let a man guard himself. Not a moment should escape, for they who allow the right moment to pass, suffer pain when they are in hell.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: They who are ashamed of what they ought not to be ashamed of, and are not ashamed of what they ought to be ashamed of, such men, embracing false doctrines enter the evil path.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: They who fear when they ought not to fear, and fear not when they ought to fear, such men, embracing false doctrines, enter the evil path.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: They who forbid when there is nothing to be forbidden, and forbid not when there is something to be forbidden, such men, embracing false doctrines, enter the evil path.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: They who know what is forbidden as forbidden, and what is not forbidden as not forbidden, such men, embracing the true doctrine, enter the good path.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Silently shall I endure abuse as the elephant in battle endures the arrow sent from the bow: for the world is ill-natured.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: They lead a tamed elephant to battle, the king mounts a tamed elephant; the tamed is the best among men, he who silently endures abuse.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Mules are good, if tamed, and noble Sindhu horses, and elephants with large tusks; but he who tames himself is better still.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: For with these animals does no man reach the untrodden country (Nirvana), where a tamed man goes on a tamed animal, viz. on his own well-tamed self.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The elephant called Dhanapalaka, his temples running with sap, and difficult to hold, does not eat a morsel when bound; the elephant longs for the elephant grove.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If a man becomes fat and a great eater, if he is sleepy and rolls himself about, that fool, like a hog fed on wash, is born again and again.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: This mind of mine went formerly wandering about as it liked, as it listed, as it pleased; but I shall now hold it in thoroughly, as the rider who holds the hook holds in the furious elephant.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Be not thoughtless, watch your thoughts! Draw yourself out of the evil way, like an elephant sunk in mud.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If a man find a prudent companion who walks with him, is wise, and lives soberly, he may walk with him, overcoming all dangers, happy, but considerate.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If a man find no prudent companion who walks with him, is wise, and lives soberly, let him walk alone, like a king who has left his conquered country behind,--like an elephant in the forest.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It is better to live alone, there is no companionship with a fool; let a man walk alone, let him commit no sin, with few wishes, like an elephant in the forest.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If an occasion arises, friends are pleasant; enjoyment is pleasant, whatever be the cause; a good work is pleasant in the hour of death; the giving up of all grief is pleasant.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Pleasant in the world is the state of a mother, pleasant the state of a father, pleasant the state of a Samana, pleasant the state of a Brahmana.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Pleasant is virtue lasting to old age, pleasant is a faith firmly rooted; pleasant is attainment of intelligence, pleasant is avoiding of sins.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The thirst of a thoughtless man grows like a creeper; he runs from life to life, like a monkey seeking fruit in the forest.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Whomsoever this fierce thirst overcomes, full of poison, in this world, his sufferings increase like the abounding Birana grass.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who overcomes this fierce thirst, difficult to be conquered in this world, sufferings fall off from him, like water-drops from a lotus leaf.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: This salutary word I tell you, `Do ye, as many as are here assembled, dig up the root of thirst, as he who wants the sweet-scented Usira root must dig up the Birana grass, that Mara (the tempter) may not crush you again and again, as the stream crushes the reeds.'
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: As a tree, even though it has been cut down, is firm so long as its root is safe, and grows again, thus, unless the feeders of thirst are destroyed, the pain (of life) will return again and again.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He whose thirst running towards pleasure is exceeding strong in the thirty-six channels, the waves will carry away that misguided man, viz. his desires which are set on passion.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The channels run everywhere, the creeper (of passion) stands sprouting; if you see the creeper springing up, cut its root by means of knowledge.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: A creature's pleasures are extravagant and luxurious; sunk in lust and looking for pleasure, men undergo (again and again) birth and decay.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Men, driven on by thirst, run about like a snared hare; held in fetters and bonds, they undergo pain for a long time, again and again.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Men, driven on by thirst, run about like a snared hare; let therefore the mendicant drive out thirst, by striving after passionlessness for himself.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who having got rid of the forest (of lust) (i.e. after having reached Nirvana) gives himself over to forest-life (i.e. to lust), and who, when removed from the forest (i.e. from lust), runs to the forest (i.e. to lust), look at that man! though free, he runs into bondage.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Wise people do not call that a strong fetter which is made of iron, wood, or hemp; far stronger is the care for precious stones and rings, for sons and a wife.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: That fetter wise people call strong which drags down, yields, but is difficult to undo; after having cut this at last, people leave the world, free from cares, and leaving desires and pleasures behind.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Those who are slaves to passions, run down with the stream (of desires), as a spider runs down the web which he has made himself; when they have cut this, at last, wise people leave the world free from cares, leaving all affection behind.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Give up what is before, give up what is behind, give up what is in the middle, when thou goest to the other shore of existence; if thy mind is altogether free, thou wilt not again enter into birth and decay.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If a man is tossed about by doubts, full of strong passions, and yearning only for what is delightful, his thirst will grow more and more, and he will indeed make his fetters strong.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If a man delights in quieting doubts, and, always reflecting, dwells on what is not delightful (the impurity of the body, &c.), he certainly will remove, nay, he will cut the fetter of Mara.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who has reached the consummation, who does not tremble, who is without thirst and without sin, he has broken all the thorns of life: this will be his last body.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who is without thirst and without affection, who understands the words and their interpretation, who knows the order of letters (those which are before and which are after), he has received his last body, he is called the great sage, the great man.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: `I have conquered all, I know all, in all conditions of life I am free from taint; I have left all, and through the destruction of thirst I am free; having learnt myself, whom shall I teach?'
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The gift of the law exceeds all gifts; the sweetness of the law exceeds all sweetness; the delight in the law exceeds all delights; the extinction of thirst overcomes all pain.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Pleasures destroy the foolish, if they look not for the other shore; the foolish by his thirst for pleasures destroys himself, as if he were his own enemy.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The fields are damaged by weeds, mankind is damaged by passion: therefore a gift bestowed on the passionless brings great reward.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The fields are damaged by weeds, mankind is damaged by hatred: therefore a gift bestowed on those who do not hate brings great reward.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The fields are damaged by weeds, mankind is damaged by vanity: therefore a gift bestowed on those who are free from vanity brings great reward.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The fields are damaged by weeds, mankind is damaged by lust: therefore a gift bestowed on those who are free from lust brings great reward.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Restraint in the eye is good, good is restraint in the ear, in the nose restraint is good, good is restraint in the tongue.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In the body restraint is good, good is restraint in speech, in thought restraint is good, good is restraint in all things. A Bhikshu, restrained in all things, is freed from all pain.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who controls his hand, he who controls his feet, he who controls his speech, he who is well controlled, he who delights inwardly, who is collected, who is solitary and content, him they call Bhikshu.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Bhikshu who controls his mouth, who speaks wisely and calmly, who teaches the meaning and the law, his word is sweet.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who dwells in the law, delights in the law, meditates on the law, follows the law, that Bhikshu will never fall away from the true law.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Let him not despise what he has received, nor ever envy others: a mendicant who envies others does not obtain peace of mind.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: A Bhikshu who, though he receives little, does not despise what he has received, even the gods will praise him, if his life is pure, and if he is not slothful.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who never identifies himself with name and form, and does not grieve over what is no more, he indeed is called a Bhikshu.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Bhikshu who acts with kindness, who is calm in the doctrine of Buddha, will reach the quiet place (Nirvana), cessation of natural desires, and happiness.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: O Bhikshu, empty this boat! if emptied, it will go quickly; having cut off passion and hatred thou wilt go to Nirvana.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Cut off the five (senses), leave the five, rise above the five. A Bhikshu, who has escaped from the five fetters, he is called Oghatinna, `saved from the flood.'
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Meditate, O Bhikshu, and be not heedless! Do not direct thy thought to what gives pleasure that thou mayest not for thy heedlessness have to swallow the iron ball (in hell), and that thou mayest not cry out when burning, `This is pain.'
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Without knowledge there is no meditation, without meditation there is no knowledge: he who has knowledge and meditation is near unto Nirvana.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: A Bhikshu who has entered his empty house, and whose mind is tranquil, feels a more than human delight when he sees the law clearly.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: As soon as he has considered the origin and destruction of the elements (khandha) of the body, he finds happiness and joy which belong to those who know the immortal (Nirvana).
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: And this is the beginning here for a wise Bhikshu: watchfulness over the senses, contentedness, restraint under the law; keep noble friends whose life is pure, and who are not slothful.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Let him live in charity, let him be perfect in his duties; then in the fulness of delight he will make an end of suffering.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: As the Vassika plant sheds its withered flowers, men should shed passion and hatred, O ye Bhikshus!
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Bhikshu whose body and tongue and mind are quieted, who is collected, and has rejected the baits of the world, he is called quiet.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Rouse thyself by thyself, examine thyself by thyself, thus self-protected and attentive wilt thou live happily, O Bhikshu!
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: For self is the lord of self, self is the refuge of self; therefore curb thyself as the merchant curbs a good horse.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Bhikshu, full of delight, who is calm in the doctrine of Buddha will reach the quiet place (Nirvana), cessation of natural desires, and happiness.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who, even as a young Bhikshu, applies himself to the doctrine of Buddha, brightens up this world, like the moon when free from clouds.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Stop the stream valiantly, drive away the desires, O Brahmana! When you have understood the destruction of all that was made, you will understand that which was not made.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If the Brahmana has reached the other shore in both laws (in restraint and contemplation), all bonds vanish from him who has obtained knowledge.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He for whom there is neither this nor that shore, nor both, him, the fearless and unshackled, I call indeed a Brahmana.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He who is thoughtful, blameless, settled, dutiful, without passions, and who has attained the highest end, him I call indeed a Brahmana.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The sun is bright by day, the moon shines by night, the warrior is bright in his armour, the Brahmana is bright in his meditation; but Buddha, the Awakened, is bright with splendour day and night.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Because a man is rid of evil, therefore he is called Brahmana; because he walks quietly, therefore he is called Samana; because he has sent away his own impurities, therefore he is called Pravragita (Pabbagita, a pilgrim).
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: No one should attack a Brahmana, but no Brahmana (if attacked) should let himself fly at his aggressor! Woe to him who strikes a Brahmana, more woe to him who flies at his aggressor!
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It advantages a Brahmana not a little if he holds his mind back from the pleasures of life; when all wish to injure has vanished, pain will cease.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who does not offend by body, word, or thought, and is controlled on these three points.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: After a man has once understood the law as taught by the Well-awakened (Buddha), let him worship it carefully, as the Brahmana worships the sacrificial fire.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: A man does not become a Brahmana by his platted hair, by his family, or by birth; in whom there is truth and righteousness, he is blessed, he is a Brahmana.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: What is the use of platted hair, O fool! what of the raiment of goat-skins? Within thee there is ravening, but the outside thou makest clean.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The man who wears dirty raiments, who is emaciated and covered with veins, who lives alone in the forest, and meditates, him I call indeed a Brahmana.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: I do not call a man a Brahmana because of his origin or of his mother. He is indeed arrogant, and he is wealthy: but the poor, who is free from all attachments, him I call indeed a Brahmana.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has cut all fetters, who never trembles, is independent and unshackled.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has cut the strap and the thong, the chain with all that pertains to it, who has burst the bar, and is awakened.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who, though he has committed no offence, endures reproach, bonds, and stripes, who has endurance for his force, and strength for his army.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who is free from anger, dutiful, virtuous, without appetite, who is subdued, and has received his last body.
rows.author: Dhammapada; translated by F. Max Müller
rows.rights_status_observed: F. Max Müller translation is public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who does not cling to pleasures, like water on a lotus leaf, like a mustard seed on the point of a needle.
