rows.text: Gotama Buddha was born nearly twenty-five centuries ago in the city of Kapila, in Northeast India.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Kapila was the principal city of the Sakya tribe, and his father was king of the tribe. _Gotama_ was his family name. _Buddha_ means _Awakened_ or _Enlightened_, that is to say, awakened or enlightened to the cause and the cure of human suffering.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Buddhist Scriptures tell us that when Gotama was born, the angels rejoiced and sang.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: An aged wise man inquired: “Why doth the company of angels rejoice?” They replied: “He that shall become Buddha is born in the village of the Sakyas for the welfare and happiness of mankind; therefore are we joyful and exceeding glad.”
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The wise man hastened to the king’s house, and said: “Where is the child?
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: And he took him in his arms, and said: “Without an equal is he! foremost among men!” Then, because he was an old man, and knew that he was soon to die, he became sorrowful and wept tears.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Said the Sakyas: “Will any harm come to the child?” “No,” replied the wise man, “this child shall one day become Buddha; out of love and pity for mankind he shall set in motion the Wheel of Religion; far and wide shall his religion be spread.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: But as for me, I have not long to live; before these things shall come to pass, death will be upon me.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Therefore am I stricken with woe, overwhelmed with sorrow, afflicted with grief.”
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
theme_evidence: Đoạn kể/miêu tả cần bối cảnh; chưa phải câu đứng độc lập.
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Seven days after Gotama was born, his mother died, and he was brought up by his aunt and step-mother.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: For ten years he lived a life of ease, in the enjoyment of all the comforts and luxuries which riches and high position could give him.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: For many centuries, it has been a common belief in India that when a human being dies, he is at once born again.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If he has lived a good life, he will be born again on earth as the child of a king or of a rich man, or in one of the heavens as a god.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If he has lived an evil life, he will be born again as a ghost, or as an animal, or in some place of torment.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: According to this belief, every person has been born and has lived and died so many times that it would be impossible to count the number.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Indeed, so far back into the past does this series of lives extend that it is impossible even to imagine a beginning of the series.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: What is more to the point, in each of these lives every person has endured much suffering and misery.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
theme_evidence: Văn bản tôn giáo/đạo đức cần giữ ngữ cảnh; không tự biến thành quy luật tâm lý hoặc cam kết kết quả.
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Said the Buddha: “In weeping over the death of sons and daughters and other dear ones, every person, in the course of his past lives, has shed tears more abundant than all the water contained in the four great oceans.”
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: And again: “The bones left by a single person in the course of his past lives would form a pile so huge that were all the mountains to be gathered up and piled in a heap, that heap of mountains would appear as nothing beside it.”
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: And again: “The head of every person has been cut off so many times in the course of his past lives, either as a human being or as an animal, as to cause him to shed blood more abundant than all the water contained in the four great oceans.”
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Yet for many centuries it has been a common belief in India.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Wise men taught that there was a way of escape, a way of salvation.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: If a person wished to avoid repeated lives of suffering and misery, he must leave home and family and friends, become a monk, and devote himself to fasting, bodily torture, and meditation.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
theme_evidence: Lời dẫn về tu khổ hạnh có fasting/bodily torture; chỉ giữ nghiên cứu lịch sử, không đưa thành lời khuyên Selflo.
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Buddhist Scriptures tell us that when Gotama was twenty-nine years old, he saw for the first time an Old Man, a Sick Man, a Dead Man, and a Monk.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The thought that in the course of his past lives he had endured old age, sickness, and death, times without number, terrified him, and he resolved to become a monk.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Leaving home and wife and son, he devoted himself for six years to fasting, bodily torture, and meditation.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Finally he became convinced that fasting and bodily torture were not the way of salvation, and abandoned the struggle.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Finally he came to understand the cause of human suffering and the cure for it.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Thus it was that he became Buddha, the Awakened, the Enlightened.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He saw that the cause of rebirth and suffering was craving for worldly pleasures and life and riches.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He saw that if this craving were uprooted, rebirth and suffering would come to an end.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He saw that this craving could be uprooted by right belief, right living, and meditation.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: For forty-five years the Buddha journeyed from place to place, preaching and teaching.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He founded an order of monks and nuns, and won many converts.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Missionaries carried his teachings from India to Ceylon and Burma and China and Tibet and Japan.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In a few hundred years the religion of the Buddha had spread over the whole of Asia.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Hundreds of millions of human beings have accepted his teachings.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In at least two respects, the teachings of the Buddha were quite remarkable.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In the first place, he insisted on the virtue of moderation.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He urged upon his hearers to avoid the two extremes of a life devoted to fasting and self-torture, and a life of self-indulgence.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In the second place, he taught that a man must love his neighbor as himself, returning good for evil and love for hatred.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
theme_evidence: Đã đọc toàn văn dòng; chủ đề xét theo ý chính, chưa xác minh nguồn/quyền để Release.
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He taught men to love all living creatures without respect of kind or person.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He taught men not to injure or kill any living creature, whether a human being or an animal, even in self-defense.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: All war, according to the teaching of the Buddha, is unholy.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In the course of time it came to be believed that Gotama had become Buddha as the fruit of good deeds performed in countless previous states of existence, especially deeds of generosity.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: At any time, had he so desired, he might have uprooted craving for worldly pleasures and life and riches by meditation, and thus have escaped the sufferings of repeated states of existence.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Out of pity and compassion and friendliness for living creatures, he preferred to be reborn again and again, to suffer and to die again and again, in order that, by the accumulated merit of good works, he might himself become enlightened and thus be able to enlighten others.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
theme_evidence: Văn bản tôn giáo/đạo đức cần giữ ngữ cảnh; không tự biến thành quy luật tâm lý hoặc cam kết kết quả.
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In comparison with the career of the Future Buddha, devoted to the performance of good works, unselfish, generous to the point of sacrificing his own body and blood,--the career of the monk, isolated from the world, selfish, seeking by meditation to uproot craving for worldly pleasures and life and riches, seemed low and mean.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Thus began the Higher Career or Vehicle of Mahāyāna or Catholic Buddhism, as distinguished from the Lower Career or Vehicle of the more primitive Hīnayāna Buddhism of the Pāli texts.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Thus did the quest of Buddhahood supplant the quest of Nibbāna.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: This development took place long before the beginning of the Christian era.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Gotama Buddha made frequent use of similes, allegories, parables, fables, and other stories, to illustrate his teachings.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: His example was imitated by his followers, and in the course of time hundreds and hundreds of stories were attributed to him on general principles.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Most of these stories were, in their original form, nothing but simple folk-tales, many of them of great antiquity.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Parallels and variants are found in the Mahābhārata, the Panchatantra, Bidpai’s Fables, the Hitopadesha, the Kathāsaritsāgara, and other fiction-collections, especially those of the Jains.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Of the twenty-six stories contained in this book, of eight of which two versions are given, eleven stories or versions of stories (6, 11, 12, 13, 16, 17 _a_, 18 _a_, 19 _a_, 20 _a_, 23 _a_, 24 _a_) are taken from the oldest canonical texts of the Buddhist Sacred Scriptures.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Of these eleven stories, the first nine are said to have been related by Gotama himself, the last two being attributed to the Buddhist sage Kumāra Kassapa.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It is highly probable that the tradition embodied in the texts regarding these eleven stories is correct.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: We may therefore feel quite certain that such remarkable parables as _Brahmadatta and the prince_ (6), _Blind men and elephant_ (13), and _The birds_ (16) were actually related by Gotama himself, in substantially the same form as that in which we now have them.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It is not at all unlikely that such a parable as _Brahmadatta and Mallika_ (8) was also related by Gotama, but of this we cannot be certain.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The approximate date of these old canonical texts is now well established.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Numerous references to the Buddhist Scriptures in the Bhābrā edict of Asoka, about 250 B.C., and in the canonical work _Kathāvatthu_, of about the same date, amply justify the statement that the texts from which these eleven stories are taken are, in their present form, at least three or four centuries anterior to the Christian era.
rows.author: Translated from Pāli by Eugene Watson Burlingame
rows.work: The Grateful Elephant and Other Stories Translated from the Pāli
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In China, in the eighth century, it entered the realm of poetry as one of the polite amusements.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The fifteenth century saw Japan ennoble it into a religion of aestheticism--Teaism.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Teaism is a cult founded on the adoration of the beautiful among the sordid facts of everyday existence.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It inculcates purity and harmony, the mystery of mutual charity, the romanticism of the social order.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It is essentially a worship of the Imperfect, as it is a tender attempt to accomplish something possible in this impossible thing we know as life.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Philosophy of Tea is not mere aestheticism in the ordinary acceptance of the term, for it expresses conjointly with ethics and religion our whole point of view about man and nature.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It is hygiene, for it enforces cleanliness; it is economics, for it shows comfort in simplicity rather than in the complex and costly; it is moral geometry, inasmuch as it defines our sense of proportion to the universe.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It represents the true spirit of Eastern democracy by making all its votaries aristocrats in taste.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The long isolation of Japan from the rest of the world, so conducive to introspection, has been highly favourable to the development of Teaism.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Our home and habits, costume and cuisine, porcelain, lacquer, painting--our very literature--all have been subject to its influence.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: No student of Japanese culture could ever ignore its presence.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It has permeated the elegance of noble boudoirs, and entered the abode of the humble.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Our peasants have learned to arrange flowers, our meanest labourer to offer his salutation to the rocks and waters.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In our common parlance we speak of the man "with no tea" in him, when he is insusceptible to the serio-comic interests of the personal drama.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Again we stigmatise the untamed aesthete who, regardless of the mundane tragedy, runs riot in the springtide of emancipated emotions, as one "with too much tea" in him.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The outsider may indeed wonder at this seeming much ado about nothing.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: But when we consider how small after all the cup of human enjoyment is, how soon overflowed with tears, how easily drained to the dregs in our quenchless thirst for infinity, we shall not blame ourselves for making so much of the tea-cup.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In the worship of Bacchus, we have sacrificed too freely; and we have even transfigured the gory image of Mars.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Why not consecrate ourselves to the queen of the Camelias, and revel in the warm stream of sympathy that flows from her altar?
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In the liquid amber within the ivory-porcelain, the initiated may touch the sweet reticence of Confucius, the piquancy of Laotse, and the ethereal aroma of Sakyamuni himself.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Those who cannot feel the littleness of great things in themselves are apt to overlook the greatness of little things in others.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The average Westerner, in his sleek complacency, will see in the tea ceremony but another instance of the thousand and one oddities which constitute the quaintness and childishness of the East to him.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: He was wont to regard Japan as barbarous while she indulged in the gentle arts of peace: he calls her civilised since she began to commit wholesale slaughter on Manchurian battlefields.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Much comment has been given lately to the Code of the Samurai,--the Art of Death which makes our soldiers exult in self-sacrifice; but scarcely any attention has been drawn to Teaism, which represents so much of our Art of Life.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Fain would we remain barbarians, if our claim to civilisation were to be based on the gruesome glory of war.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Fain would we await the time when due respect shall be paid to our art and ideals.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: When will the West understand, or try to understand, the East?
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: We Asiatics are often appalled by the curious web of facts and fancies which has been woven concerning us.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: We are pictured as living on the perfume of the lotus, if not on mice and cockroaches.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It is either impotent fanaticism or else abject voluptuousness.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Indian spirituality has been derided as ignorance, Chinese sobriety as stupidity, Japanese patriotism as the result of fatalism.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It has been said that we are less sensible to pain and wounds on account of the callousness of our nervous organisation!
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: There would be further food for merriment if you were to know all that we have imagined and written about you.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: All the glamour of the perspective is there, all the unconscious homage of wonder, all the silent resentment of the new and undefined.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: You have been loaded with virtues too refined to be envied, and accused of crimes too picturesque to be condemned.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Our writers in the past--the wise men who knew--informed us that you had bushy tails somewhere hidden in your garments, and often dined off a fricassee of newborn babes!
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Nay, we had something worse against you: we used to think you the most impracticable people on the earth, for you were said to preach what you never practiced.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Commerce has forced the European tongues on many an Eastern port.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Asiatic youths are flocking to Western colleges for the equipment of modern education.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Our insight does not penetrate your culture deeply, but at least we are willing to learn.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Some of my compatriots have adopted too much of your customs and too much of your etiquette, in the delusion that the acquisition of stiff collars and tall silk hats comprised the attainment of your civilisation.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Pathetic and deplorable as such affectations are, they evince our willingness to approach the West on our knees.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Unfortunately the Western attitude is unfavourable to the understanding of the East.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Christian missionary goes to impart, but not to receive.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Your information is based on the meagre translations of our immense literature, if not on the unreliable anecdotes of passing travellers.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It is rarely that the chivalrous pen of a Lafcadio Hearn or that of the author of "The Web of Indian Life" enlivens the Oriental darkness with the torch of our own sentiments.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Perhaps I betray my own ignorance of the Tea Cult by being so outspoken.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Its very spirit of politeness exacts that you say what you are expected to say, and no more.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: So much harm has been done already by the mutual misunderstanding of the New World and the Old, that one need not apologise for contributing his tithe to the furtherance of a better understanding.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The beginning of the twentieth century would have been spared the spectacle of sanguinary warfare if Russia had condescended to know Japan better.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: What dire consequences to humanity lie in the contemptuous ignoring of Eastern problems!
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: European imperialism, which does not disdain to raise the absurd cry of the Yellow Peril, fails to realise that Asia may also awaken to the cruel sense of the White Disaster.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: You may laugh at us for having "too much tea," but may we not suspect that you of the West have "no tea" in your constitution?
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Let us stop the continents from hurling epigrams at each other, and be sadder if not wiser by the mutual gain of half a hemisphere.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: We have developed along different lines, but there is no reason why one should not supplement the other.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: You have gained expansion at the cost of restlessness; we have created a harmony which is weak against aggression.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Will you believe it?--the East is better off in some respects than the West!
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It is the only Asiatic ceremonial which commands universal esteem.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The white man has scoffed at our religion and our morals, but has accepted the brown beverage without hesitation.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The afternoon tea is now an important function in Western society.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In the delicate clatter of trays and saucers, in the soft rustle of feminine hospitality, in the common catechism about cream and sugar, we know that the Worship of Tea is established beyond question.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The philosophic resignation of the guest to the fate awaiting him in the dubious decoction proclaims that in this single instance the Oriental spirit reigns supreme.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The earliest record of tea in European writing is said to be found in the statement of an Arabian traveller, that after the year 879 the main sources of revenue in Canton were the duties on salt and tea.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Marco Polo records the deposition of a Chinese minister of finance in 1285 for his arbitrary augmentation of the tea-taxes.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It was at the period of the great discoveries that the European people began to know more about the extreme Orient.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: At the end of the sixteenth century the Hollanders brought the news that a pleasant drink was made in the East from the leaves of a bush.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Almeida (1576), Maffeno (1588), Tareira (1610), also mentioned tea.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: In the last-named year ships of the Dutch East India Company brought the first tea into Europe.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: England welcomed it in 1650 and spoke of it as "That excellent and by all physicians approved China drink, called by the Chineans Tcha, and by other nations Tay, alias Tee."
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Like all good things of the world, the propaganda of Tea met with opposition.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Heretics like Henry Saville (1678) denounced drinking it as a filthy custom.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Jonas Hanway (Essay on Tea, 1756) said that men seemed to lose their stature and comeliness, women their beauty through the use of tea.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Its cost at the start (about fifteen or sixteen shillings a pound) forbade popular consumption, and made it "regalia for high treatments and entertainments, presents being made thereof to princes and grandees." Yet in spite of such drawbacks tea-drinking spread with marvelous rapidity.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The coffee-houses of London in the early half of the eighteenth century became, in fact, tea-houses, the resort of wits like Addison and Steele, who beguiled themselves over their "dish of tea." The beverage soon became a necessity of life--a taxable matter.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: We are reminded in this connection what an important part it plays in modern history.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Colonial America resigned herself to oppression until human endurance gave way before the heavy duties laid on Tea.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: American independence dates from the throwing of tea-chests into Boston harbour.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: There is a subtle charm in the taste of tea which makes it irresistible and capable of idealisation.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Western humourists were not slow to mingle the fragrance of their thought with its aroma.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It has not the arrogance of wine, the self-consciousness of coffee, nor the simpering innocence of cocoa.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Already in 1711, says the Spectator: "I would therefore in a particular manner recommend these my speculations to all well-regulated families that set apart an hour every morning for tea, bread and butter; and would earnestly advise them for their good to order this paper to be punctually served up and to be looked upon as a part of the tea-equipage." Samuel Johnson draws his own portrait as "a hardened and shameless tea drinker, who for twenty years diluted his meals with only the infusion of the fascinating plant; who with tea amused the evening, with tea solaced the midnight, and with tea welcomed the morning."
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Charles Lamb, a professed devotee, sounded the true note of Teaism when he wrote that the greatest pleasure he knew was to do a good action by stealth, and to have it found out by accident.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: For Teaism is the art of concealing beauty that you may discover it, of suggesting what you dare not reveal.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: It is the noble secret of laughing at yourself, calmly yet thoroughly, and is thus humour itself,--the smile of philosophy.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: All genuine humourists may in this sense be called tea-philosophers, Thackeray, for instance, and of course, Shakespeare.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The poets of the Decadence (when was not the world in decadence?), in their protests against materialism, have, to a certain extent, also opened the way to Teaism.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: Perhaps nowadays it is our demure contemplation of the Imperfect that the West and the East can meet in mutual consolation.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Taoists relate that at the great beginning of the No-Beginning, Spirit and Matter met in mortal combat.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: At last the Yellow Emperor, the Sun of Heaven, triumphed over Shuhyung, the demon of darkness and earth.
rows.author: Kakuzō Okakura
rows.rights_status_observed: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg record; jurisdiction review required for redistribution.

rows.text: The Titan, in his death agony, struck his head against the solar vault and shivered the blue dome of jade into fragments.
